nodes.summary: The Chu difference block $M^1$ is the list $1, 4, 3$, and the Chu difference block $M^2$ is the list $1, 4, 4, 3$.
nodes.title: The Chu difference blocks $M^1$ and $M^2$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the difference block $M^k$ is the list of natural numbers $1, 4, \ldots, 4, 3$ of length $k + 2$: a $1$, then $k$ copies of $4$, then a $3$.
nodes.title: Chu difference block

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $A = (0 \mid 1, 1, 2, M^k, M^{k+1}, 1, 1) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the set of partial sums, starting at $0$, of the difference sequence formed by $1, 1, 2$, the Chu difference blocks $M^k$ and $M^{k+1}$, and $1, 1$. Then $A$ is balanced: $|A + A| = |A - A|$.
nodes.title: A balanced family of Chu et al

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $A = (0 \mid 1, 1, 2, M^k, M^{k+1}, M^{k+1}, 1, 1) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the set of partial sums, starting at $0$, of the difference sequence formed by $1, 1, 2$, the Chu difference blocks $M^k$, $M^{k+1}$ and $M^{k+1}$, and $1, 1$. Then $A$ is difference-dominated: $|A + A| < |A - A|$.
nodes.title: A difference-dominated family of Chu et al

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers, let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the Chu family set with parameters $k$, $l$, $t$, and let $P = 8kl + 8l + 8$. Let $X_1$, $X_2$, $X_4$, $X_5$ be the sets of the integers $Pj + (4k + 4)i + 4$, $Pj + (4k + 4)i + 8$, $Pj + 4kl + 4l + (4k + 4)i + 8$ and $Pj + 4kl + 4l + (4k + 4)i + 12$ respectively, for $1 \le i \le l$ and $0 \le j \le t - 1$, and let $X_3$, $X_6$ be the sets of…
nodes.title: Six disjoint families in the sumset of the Chu family set

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the Chu family set with parameters $k$, $l$, $t$. Then $|A + A| \ge 11 + 6klt + 10lt + 8t$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the sumset of the Chu family set

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the Chu family set with parameters $k$, $l$, $t$. Then exactly $lt + t$ elements $d$ of $A - A$ satisfy $d \ge 6$ and $d \equiv 2 \pmod 4$; that is, exactly $lt + t$ positive differences of $A$ have the form $6 + 4m$ with $m \ge 0$ an integer.
nodes.title: Positive differences of the form 6 + 4m in the Chu family set

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the Chu family set with parameters $k$, $l$, $t$. Then $|A - A| = 11 + 6klt + 8lt + 8t$.
nodes.title: Size of the difference set of the Chu family set

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers, let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the Chu family set with parameters $k$, $l$, $t$, and let $T = t(kl + l + 1)$. Then $1 + 4i$ and $2 + 4i$ lie in $A + A$ for every integer $i$ with $0 \le i \le 2 + 2T$, and $3 + 4i$ lies in $A + A$ for every integer $i$ with $0 \le i \le 1 + 2T$.
nodes.title: Elements of the sumset of the Chu family set

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the Chu family set with parameters $k$, $l$, $t$. Then $4 + (4k + 4)i + (4kl + 4l + 4)j \in A$ for all integers $i$, $j$ with $0 \le i \le l$ and $0 \le j \le t - 1$.
nodes.title: Block starting points of the Chu family set

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers, let $A = A_{k,l,t}$ be the Kumar–Mohan–Pandey set, and put $T = t(kl + l + 1)$. Then the difference set $A - A$ contains $4i$ and $1 + 4i$ for every integer $i$ with $1 \le i \le 1 + T$, and contains $3 + 4i$ for every integer $i$ with $0 \le i \le T$.
nodes.title: Differences in the Kumar–Mohan–Pandey sets (Lemma 1)

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be positive integers, let $A = A_{k,l,t}$ be the Kumar–Mohan–Pandey set, and put $T = t(kl + l + 1)$. Then $1 + 4i \in A$ for every integer $i$ with $0 \le i \le 1 + T$, and $2 + 4T \in A$ and $4 + 4T \in A$.
nodes.title: Elements of the Kumar–Mohan–Pandey sets (Lemma 4)

nodes.summary: For $k = l = t = 1$, the Kumar–Mohan–Pandey set $A_{1,1,1}$, the set of partial sums starting from $0$ of the sequence $1, 1, 2, 1, 4, 3, 1, 1, 2, 1$, is $\{0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17\}$.
nodes.title: The Kumar–Mohan–Pandey set $A_{1,1,1}$

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$, $t$ be natural numbers, let $M^k$ be the block $1, 4, \dots, 4, 3$ with $k$ fours, and let $B$ be the concatenation of $l$ copies of $M^k$. For $j \ge 1$ let $R_1(j)$ be the sequence $1, 1$ followed by $j$ copies of $2, B, 1, 1$, and let $R_3(j)$ be the sequence $2$ followed by $j$ copies of $B, 1, 1, 2$. Then the sums of the entries of $R_1(j)$ for $1 \le j \le t$ form the same set as the sums of the…
nodes.title: Two families of runs with the same sums (Proposition 1)

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $l$, $t$, let $M^n$ be the block $1, 4, \dots, 4, 3$ with $n$ fours, and let $D$ be the sequence made of $t$ copies of the block $1, 1, 2, M^k, \dots, M^k$ (with $l$ copies of $M^k$) followed by $1, 1, 2, 1$. The set $A_{k,l,t}$ is $(0 \mid D)$, the set of partial sums of $D$ starting from $0$.
nodes.title: Kumar–Mohan–Pandey sets

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $M^n$ denote the block $1, 4, \dots, 4, 3$ with $n$ fours, and let $M_1$ be one of the sequences $(1, 1)$, $(1, 1, 2)$, $(1, 1, 2, 1)$. Let $A = (0 \mid 1, 1, 2, M^{k+1}, M^k, M_1)$ be the set of partial sums, starting from $0$, of the concatenated sequence $1, 1, 2, M^{k+1}, M^k, M_1$. Then $A$ is sum-dominated: $|A - A| < |A + A|$.
nodes.title: MSTD sets with $M^{k+1}$ before $M^k$ (Theorem 4)

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $M^n$ denote the block $1, 4, \dots, 4, 3$ with $n$ fours, and let $M_1$ be one of the sequences $(1, 1, 2)$, $(1, 1, 2, 1)$. Let $A = (0 \mid 1, 1, 2, M^k, M^{k+1}, M_1)$ be the set of partial sums, starting from $0$, of the concatenated sequence $1, 1, 2, M^k, M^{k+1}, M_1$. Then $A$ is sum-dominated: $|A - A| < |A + A|$.
nodes.title: MSTD sets with $M^k$ before $M^{k+1}$ (Theorem 3)

nodes.summary: For an integer $a$ and natural numbers $g_1, \dots, g_r$ ($r \ge 0$), write $(a \mid g_1, \dots, g_r)$ for the set of partial sums $\{a, a + g_1, \dots, a + g_1 + \dots + g_r\}$. Then for every natural number $g$, $(a \mid g, g_1, \dots, g_r) = \{a\} \cup (a + g \mid g_1, \dots, g_r)$.
nodes.title: Prepending a gap

nodes.summary: The set with least element $0$ and consecutive differences $1, 5, 1, 1, 9, 7$ is $(0 \mid 1, 5, 1, 1, 9, 7) = \{0, 1, 6, 7, 8, 17, 24\}$.
nodes.title: An example of difference notation

nodes.summary: For an integer $a$ and natural numbers $g_1, \dots, g_r$, the set $(a \mid g_1, \dots, g_r)$ is the finite set of integers $\{a, a + g_1, a + g_1 + g_2, \dots, a + g_1 + \dots + g_r\}$; for $r = 0$ it is $\{a\}$.
nodes.title: Sets given by consecutive differences

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
